Modified assessment with SLOOS context: The statement remains moderately hawkish but measured. The July 2018 SLOOS indicates banks—especially foreign banks—eased C&I lending standards and saw narrower loan rate spreads, citing the strong economic outlook and tight labor market. This points to accommodative bank credit conditions that reinforce the FOMC’s confidence in continued expansion and support the case for gradual hikes, marginally strengthening the hawkish tilt. That said, mixed demand in some categories (e.g., mortgages/consumer) tempers the tone, consistent with the Committee’s “symmetric” 2 percent inflation objective and “risks… roughly balanced.”

Net effect versus the initial read: slightly more hawkish given easier credit conditions and narrower spreads reported in SLOOS.
